upstream.note: The newest published cmark-gfm release. It is pinned only as the implementation oracle for the GFM extension layer; current CommonMark semantics come from the separately pinned cmark release.

claim: With Markdown Core's product extensions disabled, GFM extension constructs match cmark-gfm 0.29.0.gfm.13 except for the reviewed deltas below. cmark-gfm has no authority over the underlying CommonMark layer.

deltas.summary: cmark-gfm removes unreferenced footnote definitions. Markdown Core keeps every definition at its source location.
deltas.rationale: An unreferenced definition is authored source and must remain represented. remark independently keeps it.
deltas.handling: The comparison projects Markdown Core's retained definitions into cmark-gfm's resolved model before comparing.

deltas.summary: cmark-gfm moves definitions to the document tail in reference order; Markdown Core leaves them where they were written.
deltas.handling: Both sides lift definitions into a deterministic comparison-only order, preserving their content while ignoring the representation difference.

deltas.summary: cmark-gfm derives a call label from neighbouring decoded nodes using source-column lengths. Markdown Core slices the authored source between brackets.
deltas.rationale: The upstream model loses bytes across line endings and can read a freed decode buffer when the caret came from an entity. A failed call must degrade to the bytes the author wrote.
deltas.handling: Exact inputs are registered because erasing labels globally would hide valid label differences.

deltas.summary: For nested duplicate definitions cmark-gfm keeps the one that closes first and destroys the other. Markdown Core resolves in source-opening order and retains the loser as authored content.
deltas.handling: The nested witness is registered exactly so the gate continues checking both resolution and retention.

deltas.summary: cmark-gfm searches the whole line for `[x]`; Markdown Core reads only the marker the task-list scanner matched.
deltas.handling: The exact unchecked-item witness is registered; removing `checked` from every comparison would hide real task-state drift.

deltas.summary: cmark-gfm can emit empty Text nodes after extension and break processing. Markdown Core and mdast omit nodes that own no source or content.
deltas.handling: The normalizer drops empty Text nodes on both sides and records that the projection acted.

deltas.summary: cmark-gfm flattens the already-parsed interior of an undefined footnote call. Markdown Core treats it as an unmatched bracket and preserves the CommonMark inline structure inside it.
deltas.rationale: An extension construct that did not resolve must not erase structure produced by the underlying language parser. remark agrees with Markdown Core.
deltas.handling: The emphasis and strikethrough witnesses are registered exactly.

deltas.summary: When a table is recovered from a multiline paragraph, cmark-gfm pipe-unescapes the split-off non-table lead twice. Markdown Core parses the lead once as an ordinary paragraph.
deltas.rationale: The lead is not table content; remark/micromark independently preserves the same spelling as Markdown Core.
deltas.handling: The escaped-pipe witness is registered exactly.

deltas.summary: cmark-gfm consumes reference definitions into a map. Markdown Core retains source-faithful ReferenceDefinition and reference nodes.
deltas.handling: The normalizer projects Markdown Core's representation into the upstream resolved model while still comparing which definition, destination, title, and children were selected.

expectedDivergences.note: The label crosses a line ending; cmark-gfm loses the label interior.
An entity-spelled caret exposes cmark-gfm's decoded-buffer lifetime and length error.
An escaped caret is text, not the literal source marker that opens a footnote call.

expectedDivergences.input:
Ref [^dup].

[^dup]: OUTER opens first

    [^dup]: INNER closes first
expectedDivergences.note: The nested duplicate distinguishes source order from close order and checks that the losing definition survives.

expectedDivergences.input:
a[^n] b

a[\^n] b

a[^n] b

a[^n] b

a[^n] b

a[^n] b

[^n]: note
expectedDivergences.note: Only a literal source caret opens a call; decoded or escaped spellings remain ordinary text.
The later literal `[x]` must not change the unchecked marker at the start of the item.
Emphasis inside an undefined call remains parsed.
Strikethrough inside an undefined call remains parsed.
The non-table lead is parsed once, so an escaped backslash remains distinct from a pipe escape.

corpus.note: Only headings explicitly marked `(extension)` are in cmark-gfm's authority scope.
Only regressions tagged with one or more GFM extensions are selected.
Repository-owned tests for table, strikethrough, autolink, task-list, and footnote extensions.

corpusNote: This gate intentionally does not compare unextended CommonMark examples. Markdown Core runs the `gfm` profile, which attaches the cmark-gfm extension set but leaves product directive and formula syntax disabled. CommonMark is checked separately against current cmark.
